faq.q: Is Google Business Profile free in India?
faq.a: Yes. Google says you can add or claim your business at no charge. You pay only if you hire someone to manage it, or if you choose to run Google ads, which are separate from the free listing.

Google says its review takes up to 5 business days after you complete the steps, occasionally longer. Postcard codes usually arrive within 14 days and expire after 30. Some profiles are verified instantly, for example when the website is already verified in Google Search Console.

faq.q: Can I choose video verification instead of a postcard?
faq.a: No. Google picks the methods automatically from your business type, region, public information and hours, and they can't be changed. If video is offered, Google recommends it.

faq.q: Can I list my business from home?
faq.a: Yes, if you travel to customers. Set it up as a service-area business and hide the home address. If customers come to your home for the service, it needs to be staffed and open to them during your stated hours.

faq.q: Can I write my business name in Telugu and English?
faq.a: Not both together. Google's guidelines no longer allow the same name repeated in two scripts, even if your signboard shows both. Choose one script for the name, and use either language in your description, posts and replies.

faq.q: Can I offer a discount for Google reviews?
faq.a: No. Google's policy names payment, discounts and free goods or services in exchange for reviews as fake engagement. Ask every customer with a link or QR code and give nothing in return.

faq.q: How do I get a suspended profile back?
faq.a: Fix whatever broke the guidelines, then appeal through Google's appeals tool with documents whose name and address match the profile. An appeal can only be submitted once, so include everything. Don't create a new profile for the same business.

contentHtml:
What a Google Business Profile is

In short: A Google Business Profile is the free listing that shows your shop, clinic or restaurant on Google Maps and in local search results. You add or claim it at business.google.com, verify that you run the business, and then keep it accurate. Google ranks local results on relevance, distance and prominence, and you cannot pay to move up.

Google's help centre says you can add or claim your business at no charge. Anyone charging you for "registering on Google Maps" is charging for their time, not the listing.

This guide was checked in November 2026 against Google's own help pages. Google renames buttons and retires features often, so if a label below has moved, look for the nearest one.

What a profile controls and what it does not

Before any steps, the limits.

What your Business Profile gives you, and what stays out of your hands

What you wantCan you control it from the profile?
Your name, address or service area, phone, website and hoursYes, once verified
Your categories, services, photos and postsYes, within Google's content rules
Replying to reviewsYes
Removing a fair but negative reviewNo
Which photo Google shows firstPartly: Google may show a customer photo instead of your cover
Your position in the map resultsNo: there is no way to request or pay for a better local ranking
Chatting with customers inside the profileNo: chat was switched off on 31 July 2024

Source: Google's local ranking tips, Google's photo help page and Search Engine Roundtable, read 16 November 2026.

Think of the profile as your signboard on Google. You decide what is painted on it. Google decides how many people walk past.

If you would rather have the website and local search work scoped and priced before you spend on it, our ₹3,500 requirement analysis gives you a call with the people who would build it and a written quotation and timeline (how it works). Everything below works without us.

Check you are eligible first

Google's eligibility rule: a business must make in-person contact with customers during its stated hours.

Google lists online-only businesses, lead generation agents, and rental or for-sale properties such as vacant flats as ineligible.

Google's guidelines say a rented mailing address you don't operate from, a virtual office, is not eligible. An office in a co-working space only counts if it has clear signage, receives customers during business hours, and is staffed by your own people in those hours. P.O. boxes are out too.

Storefront, service-area or both

Pick the right type before you fill anything in.

Storefront. Customers come to you: a pharmacy, salon or clinic. Your address shows, and Google expects permanent signage with your name there.

Service-area. You go to customers: a plumber, a home tutor, an AC repair service. Google says to hide your address and list the areas you serve instead.

Hybrid. Both. You can show the address and add a service area, but only if the address is staffed and receives customers during your stated hours.

Google's service-area help page adds three limits. You can have up to 20 service areas. You can't draw a radius around your business. And the overall area shouldn't extend more than about 2 hours of driving time from where you are based.

Set it up step by step

Here is the order I would do it in.

Step 1. Use a Google Account you will keep. Google's verification page says you need a Google Account, and it can be a Gmail address or any email you prefer. Use one the business owns, not a staff member's personal Gmail.

Step 2. Search before you add. Your business may already be on Maps. Search your name and city in Google Maps and look for "Claim this business", then "Manage now" (in the app, it sits under About). If someone else already verified it, you request ownership instead.

Step 3. If nothing exists, add it. Go to business.google.com/add, choose "Add your business to Google", and follow the screens.

Step 4. Type the name exactly as your signboard reads. Google wants your real-world name as used on your storefront and stationery. No taglines, phone numbers or added city names. More on this under suspensions.

Step 5. Pick a category, then the address or service area. One primary category, as specific as possible. Then your address, or your service areas with the address hidden. If Google can't find your street number, drop a pin.

Step 6. Add phone, website and hours. The phone must connect to that location and be under your direct control; premium-rate numbers are not allowed. Use special hours for Diwali, Sankranti or any day you close.

Verification: the methods Google offers today

Until you verify, you can't edit your information or reply to customers. Google chooses the methods automatically, from your business type, public information, region and hours, and you can't change them. Some businesses must complete more than one.

  • Video recording. Google recommends this one if you are offered it. The recording must be at least 30 seconds, live, unedited and continuous. Show street signs or nearby businesses, your signboard, and something only staff can reach, such as the billing counter. A service business shows its tools and itself at work.
  • Live video call. A support representative watches while you show the same things. It is only available during your business hours.
  • Phone or SMS. Google sends a code. Automated phone menus (IVR) won't receive it, so make sure a person or a phone that takes texts is on that number.
  • Email. You follow the steps in an email sent to the address shown on the verification screen.
  • Postcard. Not available to every business. Most codes arrive within 14 days and expire after 30. While you wait, don't edit your name, address or category, and don't request a new code, or the one in the post stops working.

After you finish, Google says the review takes up to 5 business days. It can be instant if your website is already verified in Google Search Console. Google says it will never ask for your code.

How Google ranks local results

Google names the factors itself. Its ranking page says local results are mainly based on relevance, distance and popularity, then explains them under three headings.

Relevance is how well your profile matches what someone searched for. Complete, detailed information helps Google understand what you do.

Distance is how far you are from the person searching. If they don't share their location, Google uses what it knows about it. You can't change it, beyond placing your pin correctly.

Prominence is how well-known the business is. Google says this draws on things like how many websites link to you and how many reviews you have, and that more reviews and positive ratings can help.

Google adds that there is no way to request or pay for a better local ranking.

Whitespark's 2026 Local Search Ranking Factors survey of 47 local search specialists rated the primary category as the top map pack factor, then searcher distance, then keywords in the business name. That last one is the trap: it breaks Google's name rules. Treat the survey as expert opinion, not Google's word.

Categories: the field that does the most work

Google's guidelines give a neat test: choose categories that complete the sentence "this business IS a", not "this business HAS a". A clinic IS a dental clinic. It HAS a waiting room with Wi-Fi, which is an attribute, not a category.

Use as few categories as you need, as specific as possible. A specific category already covers the general ones behind it. Don't add categories as keywords, or for a different business inside yours.

If your exact trade isn't in the list, choose the nearest more general one. Google also reads category information from your website and mentions elsewhere on the web.

Reviews: asking, replying and what Google bans

Asking. Google's review help page says you can ask customers to visit a Google link or scan a QR code, both created from your profile. Print the QR at the counter and add the link to your bill message.

What is banned. Google's prohibited content policy is specific. It lists as fake engagement reviews "paid for, directly or in kind", and offering incentives "such as payment, discounts, free goods and/or services" for any review. It also bans content based on a conflict of interest, including current or former employment, so staff should not review their own workplace. And it bans selectively asking only happy customers while discouraging negative reviews. Ask everyone, the same way.

Replying. Google's advice: keep it short, use the reviewer's name, refer to what they said, and reply promptly. For a negative review, apologise where you were wrong, never share private details, and don't advertise offers.

One rule for review requests

Ask every customer, in the same words, with nothing given in return. If your request would change depending on whether they liked you, or comes with a discount, it breaks Google's policy.

Photos, posts, products and services

Photos. Google accepts JPG or PNG between 10 KB and 5 MB, recommends 720 by 720 pixels, and takes videos up to 30 seconds. Your cover photo is a request, not a guarantee: Google says a low-quality cover may be replaced with a customer's photo.

Posts. There are three kinds: updates, offers and events. Posts older than six months are archived unless you set a date range, and a phone number in a post may be rejected if Google can't link it to you.

Services. Businesses in some categories, mostly service businesses, can list services with an optional price and description. Custom service names must not contain prices, phone numbers or personal information.

Products. The in-store products feature, which shows what is on your shelves, is limited by Google's guidelines to the US, Canada, the UK and Ireland.

What Google has switched off

Old guides still mention features that no longer exist.

  • Chat and call history. Search Engine Roundtable reported Google's notice in May 2024: chat ended and call history reports stopped on 31 July 2024. Customers can still call you from Maps. Put your WhatsApp number on your website instead.
  • Free Business Profile websites. The sites made from profile information stopped working on 5 March 2024 and redirected to the Maps listing, and the redirects ended on 10 June 2024.
  • Public Q&A. In December 2025 Google confirmed to Search Engine Roundtable that it was essentially removing Q&A from Maps in favour of an AI-powered Ask button. I could not confirm from Google when Ask reaches every Indian user, so I would not plan around it.

Suspensions and what triggers them

A suspended profile can't be seen by the public or managed by you. The commonest trigger is the name.

Business names Google's guidelines do not accept, with Indian-style examples

What Google forbids in the nameNot acceptableAcceptable
Marketing taglinesSri Sai Sweets, Taste of TraditionSri Sai Sweets
Service or product wordsSmile Dental Root Canal SpecialistsSmile Dental
Location words not on your signboardParadise Tiffins Near Ameerpet MetroParadise Tiffins
Phone numbers or website addressesQuick Movers 98xxxxxxxxQuick Movers
HoursNandu's Pharmacy Open 24 HoursNandu's Pharmacy
The same name repeated in two scriptsLakshmi Silks / లక్ష్మి సిల్క్స్Lakshmi Silks

Source: Google's guidelines for representing your business, read 16 November 2026. The business names are invented examples, following the rule categories in Google's own table.

The other common triggers, all from the same guidelines: a virtual office or unstaffed co-working desk as your address, more than one profile for the same location, and a service-area business showing a home address it doesn't receive customers at.

Why is a competitor's stuffed name still live? A December 2020 Sterling Sky study of 50 reported keyword-stuffed listings found 60% got only a warning, 20% a soft suspension and 20% a hard one, with enforcement depending on reports. It is old, but it explains the gap.

If you are suspended. Fix the problem, gather documents whose name and address match the profile (registration, licence, tax certificate or utility bill), and use the appeals tool. An appeal can only be submitted once.

Indian specifics: languages and branches

Telugu, Hindi and the business name

Google's Business Profile help centre is available in Telugu and Hindi, if you or your manager would rather read the rules that way.

The name itself has a newer rule. Google's guidelines now list "Repeated Bilingual Names / Script Transliterations" as not allowed: the same name in two scripts, even when your signboard shows both. PinMeTo reported the change being spotted around 10 August 2026. Pick one script and use it consistently. Your description, posts and replies can use any language.

Multiple branches

One profile per location, never more. Google's chain rules say all branches should carry the same name and share the category that best represents the business, unless a branch is genuinely signed differently.

With 10 or more locations from the same business, you can apply for bulk verification from Business Profile Manager, by filling in a form.

Three worked examples

The businesses here are made up to show the method. They are not real businesses or real results.

A dental clinic

Say you run a two-chair dental clinic in Kukatpally. Name: exactly what the signboard says, with no "Root Canal and Implant Centre" added. Category: the most specific dental one Google offers.

Doctors are individual practitioners in Google's rules, and the guidelines allow a doctor's profile to include a title such as Dr. With several doctors, the clinic has its own profile and each public-facing doctor may have one, with only their name. A solo dentist at a branded clinic shares one profile named "brand: practitioner name".

Reviews: a QR code at the front desk and the link in the appointment reminder. Never offer a free cleaning for one. Our healthcare appointments page covers the booking side.

A biryani restaurant

A dine-in biryani place with a delivery counter. Google says restaurants should use the hours diners can sit and eat, or takeout hours if there is no dining.

Menu: Google says a menu link can't go straight to a third-party ordering or delivery service, and a sample menu of "popular items" shouldn't be submitted. Put your full menu on your own website and link that. Photos: your kitchen, dining room and real plates.

A cloud kitchen brand from the same kitchen needs distinct packaging and website, a hidden address and service areas, per Google's guidelines.

A coaching institute

A NEET and JEE coaching centre with one classroom building. The temptation is the name: "Vidya Academy Best NEET Coaching in Hyderabad". That is service and location information in the name, which Google's guidelines don't allow.

Google says businesses with varied schedules, naming classes, shouldn't enter those as hours. Don't type batch timings into the hours box; post each new batch with its start date instead.

Reviews from students and parents are fine. Reviews from your faculty are not, because current or former employment is a conflict of interest in Google's policy.

Five ways this goes wrong

Keywords in the name. It may rank for a while, then a competitor reports it.

Editing during verification. Changing the name, address or category while a postcard is in the post makes the code useless, per Google's own warning.

Listing a virtual office. A rented address with no staff or signage is ineligible, and it is a common reason service businesses lose their profiles.

Buying reviews or trading them for discounts. Both are named in Google's fake engagement policy.

Setting it up once and forgetting it. Wrong festival hours send people to a closed shutter.

A 15-minute weekly routine

Set a timer.

A weekly Business Profile check, split across 15 minutes

TimeWhat to doWhat you write down
First 5 minutesReply to every new review, good or badAny complaint that repeats
Next 5 minutesCheck hours, phone and special hours for the coming week's holidaysAnything Google or a user changed
Last 5 minutesAdd one real photo or one post, such as a new batch, dish or serviceWhat you posted, dated

Once a month, search your own category on Maps from your phone and see who appears around you, much as the Meta Ads Library check looks at rivals' ads.

The profile is one part of local search. A website that names your services and area, and local links, feed relevance and prominence. If you want help with that side, our SEO services page explains what we do.

Frequently asked questions

Is Google Business Profile free in India?

Yes. Google says you can add or claim your business at no charge. You pay only if you hire someone to manage it, or if you choose to run Google ads, which are separate from the free listing.

How long does verification take?

Google says its review takes up to 5 business days after you complete the steps, occasionally longer. Postcard codes usually arrive within 14 days and expire after 30. Some profiles are verified instantly, for example when the website is already verified in Google Search Console.

Can I choose video verification instead of a postcard?

No. Google picks the methods automatically from your business type, region, public information and hours, and they can't be changed. If video is offered, Google recommends it.

Can I list my business from home?

Yes, if you travel to customers. Set it up as a service-area business and hide the home address. If customers come to your home for the service, it needs to be staffed and open to them during your stated hours.

Can I write my business name in Telugu and English?

Not both together. Google's guidelines no longer allow the same name repeated in two scripts, even if your signboard shows both. Choose one script for the name, and use either language in your description, posts and replies.

Can I offer a discount for Google reviews?

No. Google's policy names payment, discounts and free goods or services in exchange for reviews as fake engagement. Ask every customer with a link or QR code and give nothing in return.

How do I get a suspended profile back?

Fix whatever broke the guidelines, then appeal through Google's appeals tool with documents whose name and address match the profile. An appeal can only be submitted once, so include everything. Don't create a new profile for the same business.
